title: Google says its new Gemini 3.8 Flash model ‘works harder’ but might cost more
content:
Google launched Gemini 3.8 Flash, arriving just a few weeks after its predecessor. The company claims the new model “works harder” than Gemini 3.7 Flash by performing more reasoning steps on complex tasks and “calling tools iteratively.” It has the same introductory pricing as 3.7 Flash, $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens, but could still end up costing users more. Google warns that “the model might use more tokens to maximize performance, especially at higher effort levels.” Developers can keep using Gemini 3.7 Flash if they want to minimize token usage.
Google says its new Gemini 3.8 Flash model ‘works harder’ but might cost more
Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber is also launching to Google’s new Fairwind Program.
Gemini 3.8 Flash’s launch was followed by some early impressions online. Artificial Analysis highlighted the model’s pricing, saying Gemini 3.8 Flash is “the cheapest we’ve measured at this level of intelligence. This is up ~40% from Gemini 3.7 Flash despite unchanged per-token pricing, driven by a 30% increase in output tokens per task and more turns on agentic evaluations.”
Aigora.ai CEO John Ennis compared Gemini 3.8 Flash to Anthropic’s models, saying it offers “Opus 5 coding quality but at a fraction of the cost and super fast,” adding, “This is going to be so awesome for things like making remotion videos.”
Google says Gemini 3.8 Flash offers “significant improvements” for software engineering and autonomous AI agents. It outperforms its predecessor and other frontier models on the DeepSWE v1.1 software engineering benchmark, including Anthropic’s Fable 5, which got an upgrade earlier this week that also promises stronger performance at a lower price, by cutting the price to use cached data.
Google’s new model also outperformed its competitors on the Vals Finance Agent V2 benchmark and Harvey’s Legal Agent benchmark. However, the new model also “ships with safeguards against misuse in the domains of Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) and cyber offense.”
Google also released Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber alongside its new Fairwind Program, which is limited to governments and “trusted partners.” The program, whose 650 members include CrowdStrike and the Center for Internet Security, offers access to 3.8 Flash Cyber and Google’s CodeMender agent, which Google says can help “autonomously find and fix vulnerabilities, protecting critical infrastructure, public services, and national security.” Gemini 3.8 Flash is available now for consumers with a Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription, as well as developers and enterprise users.

report.summary: Google launches Gemini 3.8 Flash with deeper reasoning and tool use; same pricing but possible higher token usage and costs.
report.background: Gemini 3.8 Flash arrives only a few weeks after Google's 3.7 Flash, reflecting the accelerated release cycle in the frontier AI market. Google positions the model as one that 'works harder' on complex tasks by performing additional reasoning steps and iteratively using tools. Per-token pricing remains unchanged, but Google warns that real-world costs may rise because the model can consume more tokens at higher effort levels. Early analysis indicates that despite identical list prices, total cost per task could jump about 40% due to longer outputs and more agent turns. Google also emphasizes large gains on software engineering and agentic benchmarks, while launching a separate Cyber model through the Fairwind Program for governments and trusted partners. The release intensifies competition with Anthropic, especially after Anthropic's Fable 5 upgrade and price cut for cached data.
key_points: Google claims Gemini 3.8 Flash 'works harder' by performing more reasoning steps and iteratively calling tools on complex tasks. It arrives only weeks after Gemini 3.7 Flash and keeps the same list price: $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens.

Despite unchanged per-token pricing, costs may rise. Artificial Analysis measured total cost per task up about 40% versus 3.7 Flash, driven by roughly 30% more output tokens per task and additional turns in agentic evaluations. Developers who want to minimize token usage can stay on Gemini 3.7 Flash.

The model shows significant gains in software engineering and autonomous agent benchmarks. It outperforms its predecessor and Anthropic's Fable 5 on DeepSWE v1.1, and also leads finance and legal agent evaluations such as Vals Finance Agent V2 and Harvey's Legal Agent benchmark.

Google also released Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber through the Fairwind Program, limited to governments and trusted partners. It includes access to CodeMender, an agent that autonomously finds and fixes vulnerabilities. Google says safeguards prevent misuse in CBRN and cyber offense domains.

Gemini 3.8 Flash is available now to consumers through Google AI Pro or Ultra subscriptions, plus developers and enterprise users. Early reviewers compare its coding quality to Anthropic's Opus 5 at lower cost, while noting it is fast enough for video generation workflows.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Gemini 3.8 Flash signals that frontier performance no longer depends on premium list prices; efficiency and agentic behavior now determine real-world costs. Developers building agents should model total token consumption, not per-token pricing, because 'works harder' means larger bills. Enterprises choosing between Google and Anthropic should benchmark their own tasks using agentic evaluations, not single-turn tests. For regular users, Google AI Pro or Ultra subscribers get a more capable assistant for complex engineering work, but may see higher usage behind the scenes. The Cyber and Fairwind Program also highlights a growing split between consumer AI and restricted government or security offerings, raising questions about transparency while positioning Google as a national security provider.
report.tools: Developers can try Gemini 3.8 Flash through Google AI Studio or the Gemini API. For building agentic applications that call tools iteratively, watch LangGraph, CrewAI, or AutoGen. Google's CodeMender agent is part of the Fairwind Program, but ordinary users can explore open-source vulnerability-fixing tools such as Semgrep or CodeQL. Benchmark projects like DeepSWE and Vals provide ways to measure model performance and cost per task.
